N072_check_01 — Targeted check prompted by the written bound codim(Z,S)≥1. Put A=Q[t], S=Spec A, Z=V(t), and D=div(t). The localization A→A[t^{-1}] sends t to a unit, so the effective Cartier divisor D restricts to zero on S'=Spec A[t^{-1}]=S\Z. In A, t is a nonzero nonunit and A/(t)=Q, so D is nonzero. The prime chain (0)⊊(t), and the absence of an intervening prime in the principal ideal domain Q[t], give codim(Z,S)=1. Thus the displayed lower bound 1 and the vanishing restriction occur in this concrete example with nonzero D. This checks the isolated divisor inference, not the source's extension argument. Scan071 already specifies Z of codimension≥2; that stronger context remains in the manuscript. The transcription preserves the clearly written 1 on scan072.
